reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 19. Nay or No: 20. Not Voting: 1. votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
votes.plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards (H RES 1498)
votes.plain_language: This resolution censures Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. A Yea votes to censure him. A Nay votes not to.

lobbying.bill_title: In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards.

votes.question: On Passage — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: This bill moves the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. This vote would have delayed that bill until the Commerce Secretary published a report on how trade fights with Canada and China, and the war in Iran, affect fishing costs and seafood prices. A Yea would have added that delay; a Nay rejected it.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
votes.plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 210)
votes.bill_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision".
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that let California tighten emissions rules for ocean-going ships while they are docked. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes Environmental Protection Agency grants through fiscal year 2029 to replace old diesel engines or add pollution controls. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act (H R 1346)
votes.bill_title: To amend the Clean Air Act with respect to the ethanol waiver for Reid Vapor Pressure under that Act, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This bill amends the Clean Air Act to address the limitations on Reid Vapor Pressure (a measure of gasoline's volatility) that are placed on gasoline during the summer ozone season. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act (H R 1346)
votes.bill_title: To amend the Clean Air Act with respect to the ethanol waiver for Reid Vapor Pressure under that Act, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: H.R. 1346 amends the Clean Air Act to address the limitations on Reid Vapor Pressure (a measure of gasoline's volatility) that are placed on gasoline during the summer ozone season. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — FIRE Act (H R 6387)
votes.plain_language: This bill modifies the definition of exceptional events under the Clean Air Act and requires the Environmental Protection Agency to revise its regulations regarding exceptional events or actions to mitigate wildfire risk. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — FIRE Act (H R 6387)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6387 (FIRE Act) modifies the definition of exceptional events under the Clean Air Act and requires the Environmental Protection Agency to revise its regulations regarding exceptional events or actions to mitigate wildfire risk. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — RED Tape Act (H R 6398)
votes.plain_language: This bill removes the requirement under the Clean Air Act that the Environmental Protection Agency review and comment on newly authorized federal construction projects and other major federal agency actions that already require review under the National Environmental Policy Act and proposed federal regulations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

posts.text:
BREAKING: ICE finally released this 8 year-old boy who was detained and taken from his uncle in San Diego. I'm so relieved that tonight, the boy is back home with his family.

Thank you to everyone who raised your voices and pressured DHS to bring him home — it mattered. https://t.co/Yk8dDoTFmD

Rent prices are continuing to rise across southern California (and nationwide). We can’t afford incremental policy changes. We need bold, transformative solutions that give renters relief and rapidly scale up building.
https://t.co/DMxAXfHpcd

Young people are demanding change. We need to listen to them.

For almost their entire lives, Gen Z has watched their government fail them over and over again. If we want to win back their trust and restore hope, Democrats must deliver this time.
https://t.co/hkOhl3aNEv

It was great to visit Patrick Henry High School to meet these students and answer their questions about Congress and politics. I also met Dr. Cecil Nedelec and her French class to talk about my work in international affairs! https://t.co/cdTvbftBdM

San Ysidro Health is a non-profit that provides health care across San Diego County, including at this clinic in El Cajon. Patients here, like so many nationwide, are paying the price for the Big Ugly Bill. We need to reinvest in health care and ensure everyone can access and afford it.

I visited the USC Alzheimer’s Therapeutic Research Institute here in San Diego to learn about their cutting edge research focused on early detection, prevention, and treatment for Alzheimer’s disease. We need to restore federal funding for critical medical research like this. https://t.co/l3PcWAKAzk

Under Trump, the Department of Homeland Security has repeatedly broken the law and violated court orders that were supposed to protect vulnerable people from being deported to countries where they faced persecution. We must hold them accountable for this.
https://t.co/9wB7F24OmH

Americans resoundingly rejected Trump’s cruel mass deportation policies on Election Day. Stephen Miller and Trump may try to continue weaponizing ICE, but a reckoning is coming. Democrats in Congress WILL use our power to hold them accountable.
https://t.co/LxLsPKNA2J

It was my honor to join The Center to induct 4 new San Diegans to their LGBT Veterans Wall of Honor. Thank you for your courage, sacrifice, and unwavering service to our country, even in the face of hatred and injustice. https://t.co/ft9rT57nXy

Thank you to every U.S. veteran for your service and countless sacrifices. I’m so proud to represent San Diego, one of the largest veteran communities in the country and I’ll keep fighting in Congress to make sure we deliver the resources and support our veterans deserve.

Republicans just voted to protect Secretary Hegseth from impeachment and rubber stamp his illegal actions, including the Iran war that's killed more than 20 service members, injured over 800, and cost us billions.

This isn’t over. Pete Hegseth is unfit, dangerous and must be https://t.co/y3iAqsXNAH

I’m working with the San Diego congressional delegation and our CA Senators to demand answers from DHS about the 8 year-old boy who was taken into federal custody at an ICE check-in last week.

We must keep fighting to ensure his safety and bring him home. https://t.co/qsM2mothZA

To be clear, these cuts are not even part of the devastating cuts to food assistance from the Big Ugly Bill that Republicans passed last year. The Trump Administration is voluntarily proposing to let millions more Americans go hungry – just because. How evil.

Secretary Pete Hegseth has repeatedly broken the law and put our service members in impossible and dangerous positions. And now, he’s blatantly trying to use them as a shield to protect himself from getting impeached by the House — which will happen. His time is up. https://t.co/bebKlKlgmt

I will vote YES to impeach Secretary Pete Hegseth. His rap sheet includes the illegal Iran war, illegal strikes in Yemen (where he mishandled classified information via Signal), and over 200 murders in boat strikes in the Caribbean and Pacific. He’s dangerous and needs to go. https://t.co/sRBUaJLSRQ

This is outrageous and unacceptable. No child should have to endure the trauma of being separated from their family and detained by ICE.

I’m working with the San Diego Congressional delegation to demand answers and bring this 8-year old boy home.
https://t.co/JANB6hJV5Q
Happy Diwali to everyone celebrating in San Diego and across the country! May this holiday bring you hope and remind us that light always triumphs over darkness.

Broad-based, pro-democracy movements – just like the one we’ve been building here in the U.S. – have the power to topple regimes. There is hope.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
